answer: Each identity takes a rung on a spiral terrace and locks a 70-credit bond. Its rung holds a juniper sapling; fees climb one step per claim: first 36, k-th 36+6(k-1), so 1,000 fakes pay 3,033,000 vs a 40,000 pool. At dawn an auditor re-measures saplings against the growth table; a short or reused reading burns it. Rented saplings fail: key-bound to owners, and dawn readings can't be pre-made. An honest agent pays 36 once; a clean audit returns it.
